grammar.n5.07.1.idea: ませんか offers an invitation that the other person can accept or decline.
grammar.n5.07.1.exercise.success: のみませんか invites someone to drink tea together; it does not state a past action or forbid it.
grammar.n5.07.1.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. のみませんか invites someone to drink tea together; it does not state a past action or forbid it.
grammar.n5.07.1.preview: いっしょにたべませんか。 — Shall we eat together?
grammar.n5.07.2.title: ましょう — suggestion
grammar.n5.07.2.rule: Replace ます with ましょう to suggest a shared action. Compared with ませんか, it presents “let us” more directly. It is not a command directed only at the other person.
grammar.n5.07.2.example.0: いきましょう。 — Let us go.
grammar.n5.07.2.example.1: ここでたべましょう。 — Let us eat here.
grammar.n5.07.2.idea: Stem + ましょう: let us do the action.
grammar.n5.07.2.exercise.question: Suggest “Let us read together”.
grammar.n5.07.2.exercise.success: よみましょう suggests reading together.
grammar.n5.07.2.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. よみましょう suggests reading together.
grammar.n5.07.2.preview: いきましょう。 — Let us go.
grammar.n5.07.3.title: ましょうか — offer
grammar.n5.07.3.goal: Offer help or suggest an action as a question.
grammar.n5.07.3.rule: Stem + ましょうか can offer to do something for someone else. Context distinguishes an offer of help from a shared suggestion.
grammar.n5.07.3.example.0: かばんをもちましょうか。 — Shall I carry your bag?
grammar.n5.07.3.example.1: まどをあけましょうか。 — Shall I open the window?
grammar.n5.07.3.idea: ましょうか asks whether you should do the action.
grammar.n5.07.3.exercise.question: Offer to close the door.
grammar.n5.07.3.exercise.prompt: ドアをしめ＿。 · しめます = close
grammar.n5.07.3.exercise.success: しめましょうか offers to close the door and awaits the other person's reply.
grammar.n5.07.3.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. しめましょうか offers to close the door and awaits the other person's reply.
grammar.n5.07.3.preview: かばんをもちましょうか。 — Shall I carry your bag?
grammar.n5.07.4.title: ないでください
grammar.n5.07.4.goal: Ask someone not to do an action.
grammar.n5.07.4.rule: Add でください to the negative ない form. This requests not doing something, unlike the affirmative request てください. Do not build it from the affirmative て form.
grammar.n5.07.4.example.0: ここでたべないでください。 — Please do not eat here.
grammar.n5.07.4.example.1: いかないでください。 — Please do not leave.
grammar.n5.07.4.idea: Negative ない + でください.
grammar.n5.07.4.exercise.success: Use はなさない and add でください. はなしてください actually asks someone to speak.
grammar.n5.07.4.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. Use はなさない and add でください. はなしてください actually asks someone to speak.
grammar.n5.07.4.preview: ここでたべないでください。 — Please do not eat here.
grammar.n5.07.5.title: なくてはいけない
grammar.n5.07.5.goal: Express that an action must be done.
grammar.n5.07.5.example.0: べんきょうしなくてはいけません。 — I have to study.
grammar.n5.07.5.example.1: くすりをのまなくてはいけません。 — I have to take the medicine.
grammar.n5.07.5.idea: ない → なくてはいけない: you must do it, not a prohibition.
grammar.n5.07.5.preview: べんきょうしなくてはいけません。 — I have to study.
grammar.n5.07.6.title: なくてはならない
grammar.n5.07.6.rule: It is formed like なくてはいけない, but ends in ならない. It means having to do something and usually sounds more formal or written. Here we focus on recognizing it without overstating the difference.
grammar.n5.07.6.example.0: いかなくてはなりません。 — I have to go.
grammar.n5.07.6.example.1: べんきょうしなくてはならない。 — You have to study.
grammar.n5.07.6.idea: なくてはならない also expresses obligation.
grammar.n5.07.6.exercise.question: Recognize the meaning of the sentence.
grammar.n5.07.6.exercise.prompt: かえらなくてはなりません。 · かえる = return
grammar.n5.07.6.exercise.success: なくてはなりません is the polite variant of an expression of obligation.
grammar.n5.07.6.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. なくてはなりません is the polite variant of an expression of obligation.
grammar.n5.07.6.preview: いかなくてはなりません。 — I have to go.
grammar.n5.07.7.title: ないと・なきゃ・なくちゃ
grammar.n5.07.7.rule: Parts of an obligation expression may be omitted in conversation. いかないと, いかなきゃ and いかなくちゃ can mean “I have to go”. Recognize the context; ないと also has other uses covered later.
grammar.n5.07.7.example.0: もう、いかなきゃ。 — I have to go now.
grammar.n5.07.7.example.1: べんきょうしなくちゃ。 — I have to study.
grammar.n5.07.7.idea: These shortened forms express obligation when context indicates it.
grammar.n5.07.7.exercise.question: In a dialogue, someone looks at the clock and says this. What do they mean?
grammar.n5.07.7.exercise.prompt: もう、かえらないと。 · かえる = return
grammar.n5.07.7.exercise.success: As a shortened sentence in that context, かえらないと means they have to return.
grammar.n5.07.7.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. As a shortened sentence in that context, かえらないと means they have to return.
grammar.n5.07.7.preview: もう、いかなきゃ。 — I have to go now.
grammar.n5.07.8.title: たほうがいい
grammar.n5.07.8.goal: Give advice to do an action.
grammar.n5.07.8.rule: た form + ほうがいいです advises doing something. た belongs to the pattern: the advice concerns what is best to do now or later, not necessarily a past action.
grammar.n5.07.8.example.0: やすんだほうがいいです。 — You should rest.
grammar.n5.07.8.example.1: はやくねたほうがいいです。 — It is better to go to bed early.
grammar.n5.07.8.idea: Use the た form for this affirmative advice.
grammar.n5.07.8.preview: やすんだほうがいいです。 — You should rest.
grammar.n5.07.9.title: ないほうがいい
grammar.n5.07.9.rule: Negative ない form + ほうがいいです recommends not doing something. This is advice, not a prohibition. Do not use the negative past なかった for this pattern.
grammar.n5.07.9.example.0: ここでたべないほうがいいです。 — It is better not to eat here.
grammar.n5.07.9.example.1: コーヒーをのまないほうがいいです。 — It is better not to drink coffee.
grammar.n5.07.9.idea: ないほうがいい: it is better not to do it.
grammar.n5.07.9.exercise.question: Advise not going today.
grammar.n5.07.9.exercise.prompt: きょうはいく → negative advice
grammar.n5.07.9.exercise.option.0: いかなかったほうがいいです。
grammar.n5.07.9.exercise.option.1: いかないほうがいいです。
grammar.n5.07.9.exercise.success: いかないほうがいい advises not going. いってはいけません is a prohibition, not the requested advice.
grammar.n5.07.9.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. いかないほうがいい advises not going. いってはいけません is a prohibition, not the requested advice.
grammar.n5.07.9.preview: ここでたべないほうがいいです。 — It is better not to eat here.
grammar.n5.07.10.title: たい — desire to do an action
grammar.n5.07.10.goal: Express what you want to do.
grammar.n5.07.10.rule: Remove ます and add たい. The resulting form behaves like an い adjective: たくない, たかった. Here it expresses your own desire; do not use this pattern to assert another person's feelings without context.
grammar.n5.07.10.example.0: にほんにいきたいです。 — I want to go to Japan.
grammar.n5.07.10.example.1: パンをたべたくないです。 — I do not want to eat bread.
grammar.n5.07.10.idea: ます stem + たい: desire to do an action.
grammar.n5.07.10.exercise.prompt: このほんを＿です。 · よみます = read
grammar.n5.07.10.exercise.success: Remove ます from よみます and add たい: よみたい.
grammar.n5.07.10.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. Remove ます from よみます and add たい: よみたい.
grammar.n5.07.10.preview: にほんにいきたいです。 — I want to go to Japan.
grammar.n5.07.11.title: がほしい — desire for an object
grammar.n5.07.11.goal: Distinguish wanting something from wanting to do something.
grammar.n5.07.11.rule: Noun + がほしいです expresses wanting an object. ほしい is an い adjective. For an action, use stem + たい; do not place a verb directly before がほしい.
grammar.n5.07.11.example.0: あたらしいかばんがほしいです。 — I want a new bag.
grammar.n5.07.11.example.1: ほんがほしいです。 — I want a book.
grammar.n5.07.11.idea: Object がほしい; action with ます stem + たい.
grammar.n5.07.11.exercise.success: みず is an object: がほしいです. To want to drink, you would use のみたいです.
grammar.n5.07.11.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. みず is an object: がほしいです. To want to drink, you would use のみたいです.
grammar.n5.07.11.preview: あたらしいかばんがほしいです。 — I want a new bag.
grammar.n5.07.journey.title: Learn step by step
grammar.n5.07.practice.title: Topic 07 review
grammar.n5.07.practice.body: Mix what you have learned with new examples. Read the whole sentence before choosing; the feedback explains each answer.
grammar.n5.07.practice.0.question: Choose an invitation to go to the park together.
grammar.n5.07.practice.0.prompt: いっしょにこうえんに＿。
grammar.n5.07.practice.0.success: いきませんか invites someone to go together.
grammar.n5.07.practice.0.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. いきませんか invites someone to go together.
grammar.n5.07.practice.1.question: Suggest “Let's drink coffee”.
grammar.n5.07.practice.1.success: ましょう suggests doing the action together.
grammar.n5.07.practice.1.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. ましょう suggests doing the action together.
grammar.n5.07.practice.2.question: Offer to carry a book.
grammar.n5.07.practice.2.prompt: ほんをもち＿。 · もちます = carry
grammar.n5.07.practice.2.success: もちましょうか offers help as a question.
grammar.n5.07.practice.2.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. もちましょうか offers help as a question.
grammar.n5.07.practice.3.question: Ask someone not to close the window.
grammar.n5.07.practice.3.prompt: まどを＿ください。 · しめる = close
grammar.n5.07.practice.3.success: The negative request uses ないでください.
grammar.n5.07.practice.3.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. The negative request uses ないでください.
grammar.n5.07.practice.5.question: What does it mean?
grammar.n5.07.practice.5.prompt: はやくねなくてはならない。
grammar.n5.07.practice.5.option.0: Going to sleep early is not allowed.
grammar.n5.07.practice.5.option.1: I have already gone to sleep early.
grammar.n5.07.practice.5.option.2: You have to go to sleep early.
grammar.n5.07.practice.5.success: なくてはならない is another form of obligation.
grammar.n5.07.practice.5.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. なくてはならない is another form of obligation.
grammar.n5.07.practice.6.question: In this context, what does it mean?
grammar.n5.07.practice.6.prompt: I have an exam tomorrow: べんきょうしないと。
grammar.n5.07.practice.6.success: The contextual shortened form しないと expresses obligation.
grammar.n5.07.practice.6.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. The contextual shortened form しないと expresses obligation.
grammar.n5.07.practice.7.question: Give advice to rest.
grammar.n5.07.practice.7.option.0: やすみほうがいいです。
grammar.n5.07.practice.7.option.1: やすんだほうがいいです。
grammar.n5.07.practice.7.option.2: やすんでほうがいいです。
grammar.n5.07.practice.7.success: Affirmative advice in this pattern uses the た form: やすんだ.
grammar.n5.07.practice.7.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. Affirmative advice in this pattern uses the た form: やすんだ.
grammar.n5.07.practice.8.question: Give advice not to buy.
grammar.n5.07.practice.8.option.1: かわなかったほうがいいです。
grammar.n5.07.practice.8.option.2: かわないほうがいいです。
grammar.n5.07.practice.8.success: ないほうがいい advises avoiding the action; てはいけません prohibits it.
grammar.n5.07.practice.8.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. ないほうがいい advises avoiding the action; てはいけません prohibits it.
grammar.n5.07.practice.9.question: Choose “I want a pen, and I want to write”.
grammar.n5.07.practice.9.prompt: ペン = pen · かきます = write
grammar.n5.07.practice.9.option.0: ペンがほしいです。かきたいです。
grammar.n5.07.practice.9.option.2: ペンをほしいたいです。
grammar.n5.07.practice.9.success: The object uses がほしい; the action uses verb stem + たい.
grammar.n5.07.practice.9.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. The object uses がほしい; the action uses verb stem + たい.
grammar.n5.08.1.title: から — reason
grammar.n5.08.1.goal: Link a reason to what happens because of it.
grammar.n5.08.1.rule: から after a sentence introduces a reason. Put the reason first, then the consequence. With nouns or な adjectives in the affirmative plain form, use だから. This differs from から indicating origin.
grammar.n5.08.1.example.0: あついですから、みずをのみます。 — Because it is hot, I drink water.
grammar.n5.08.1.example.1: ひまだから、ほんをよむ。 — Because I am free, I read a book.
grammar.n5.08.1.exercise.prompt: たかいです＿、かいません。
grammar.n5.08.1.preview: あついですから、みずをのみます。 — Because it is hot, I drink water.
grammar.n5.08.2.title: ので — reason
grammar.n5.08.2.goal: Give a reason with a softer connection.
grammar.n5.08.2.rule: ので links a reason to its consequence and usually presents it more softly or descriptively. It attaches to the plain form; affirmative non-past nouns and な adjectives use なので. There is no absolute distinction from から.
grammar.n5.08.2.example.0: あめがふるので、うちにいます。 — Because it is raining, I am at home.
grammar.n5.08.2.example.1: しずかなので、ここでべんきょうします。 — Because it is quiet, I study here.
grammar.n5.08.2.idea: Plain form + ので; noun/な adjective + なので.
grammar.n5.08.2.exercise.question: Complete “Because I am free, I am going”.
grammar.n5.08.2.exercise.success: ひま is a な adjective: use なので for this connection.
grammar.n5.08.2.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. ひま is a な adjective: use なので for this connection.
grammar.n5.08.2.preview: あめがふるので、うちにいます。 — Because it is raining, I am at home.
grammar.n5.08.3.title: けど — contrast
grammar.n5.08.3.goal: Connect two contrasting ideas in conversation.
grammar.n5.08.3.rule: けど connects sentences with a contrast like “but”. It can follow a polite or plain form; with an affirmative plain noun or な adjective, use だけど. Here we practise explicit contrast between two sentences.
grammar.n5.08.3.example.0: たかいですけど、おいしいです。 — It is expensive, but tasty.
grammar.n5.08.3.example.1: ちいさいけど、べんりです。 — It is small, but useful.
grammar.n5.08.3.preview: たかいですけど、おいしいです。 — It is expensive, but tasty.
grammar.n5.08.4.title: が — but
grammar.n5.08.4.goal: Recognize が after a sentence as a connector.
grammar.n5.08.4.rule: が after a complete sentence can mean “but”. It is not the が that marks a thing or person before the predicate. Distinguish its function by position and context.
grammar.n5.08.4.example.0: おいしいですが、たかいです。 — It is tasty, but expensive.
grammar.n5.08.4.example.1: いきたいですが、じかんがありません。 — I want to go, but I have no time.
grammar.n5.08.4.idea: Complete sentence + が、another sentence: a contrast connection.
grammar.n5.08.4.exercise.question: What function does the first が have?
grammar.n5.08.4.exercise.prompt: このほんはおもしろいですが、むずかしいです。
grammar.n5.08.4.exercise.success: After おもしろいです, が links a contrast with むずかしいです.
grammar.n5.08.4.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. After おもしろいです, が links a contrast with むずかしいです.
grammar.n5.08.4.preview: おいしいですが、たかいです。 — It is tasty, but expensive.
grammar.n5.08.5.title: や — open list
grammar.n5.08.5.goal: List examples without saying they are all the items.
grammar.n5.08.5.rule: や connects nouns as examples in an open list. と presents a complete list in the basic context: A and B. や implies that there may be other things.
grammar.n5.08.5.example.0: パンやくだものをかいます。 — I buy bread, fruit and things like that.
grammar.n5.08.5.example.1: ほんとノートをかいます。 — I buy a book and a notebook.
grammar.n5.08.5.idea: や gives examples; と joins the items you present as a complete list.
grammar.n5.08.5.exercise.success: や presents おちゃ and コーヒー as examples without closing the list.
grammar.n5.08.5.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. や presents おちゃ and コーヒー as examples without closing the list.
grammar.n5.08.5.preview: パンやくだものをかいます。 — I buy bread, fruit and things like that.
grammar.n5.08.6.title: だけ — only
grammar.n5.08.6.goal: Limit what you include in a statement.
grammar.n5.08.6.rule: だけ after a noun means only that item. Keep the particles the sentence needs: ひとりだけ, only one person; みずだけを, only water as the object.
grammar.n5.08.6.example.0: みずだけをのみます。 — I drink only water.
grammar.n5.08.6.example.1: ひとりだけいます。 — There is only one person.
grammar.n5.08.6.idea: だけ limits the noun before it.
grammar.n5.08.6.exercise.question: What does the sentence indicate?
grammar.n5.08.6.exercise.prompt: りんごだけをかいました。
grammar.n5.08.6.exercise.option.0: I bought many kinds of fruit.
grammar.n5.08.6.exercise.success: だけ restricts the purchase to りんご, apples.
grammar.n5.08.6.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. だけ restricts the purchase to りんご, apples.
grammar.n5.08.6.preview: みずだけをのみます。 — I drink only water.
grammar.n5.08.7.title: たり・たりする
grammar.n5.08.7.goal: Present representative activities without a fixed order.
grammar.n5.08.7.rule: Start from the た form and add り to each activity: たべたり、のんだりします. The final する carries tense and politeness. These are examples of activities, not a strict sequence as with て.
grammar.n5.08.7.example.0: ほんをよんだり、えいがをみたりします。 — I read, watch films and things like that.
grammar.n5.08.7.example.1: たべたり、のんだりしました。 — We ate, drank and things like that.
grammar.n5.08.7.idea: た form + り; repeat and end with する.
grammar.n5.08.7.preview: ほんをよんだり、えいがをみたりします。 — I read, watch films and things like that.
grammar.n5.08.8.title: もう — already
grammar.n5.08.8.goal: Indicate that an action is already complete.
grammar.n5.08.8.rule: In the pattern we practise, もう + past states that something has already happened. Do not confuse it with まだ, still. もう has other meanings depending on context, but here we recognize “already”.
grammar.n5.08.8.example.0: もうたべました。 — I have already eaten.
grammar.n5.08.8.example.1: もううちにかえりました。 — I have already returned home.
grammar.n5.08.8.idea: もう + past: the action has already happened.
grammar.n5.08.8.exercise.question: What does the answer state?
grammar.n5.08.8.exercise.prompt: もうほんをよみました。
grammar.n5.08.8.exercise.option.0: I have already read the book.
grammar.n5.08.8.exercise.option.1: I have not read the book yet.
grammar.n5.08.8.exercise.success: もう with よみました presents reading the book as complete.
grammar.n5.08.8.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. もう with よみました presents reading the book as complete.
grammar.n5.08.8.preview: もうたべました。 — I have already eaten.
grammar.n5.08.9.title: まだ — still
grammar.n5.08.9.goal: Indicate that a situation remains true.
grammar.n5.08.9.rule: まだ with an affirmative statement signals continuity. What was true before still is. Its meaning changes in negative patterns that we will see next.
grammar.n5.08.9.example.0: まだあついです。 — It is still hot.
grammar.n5.08.9.example.1: まだべんきょうしています。 — I am still studying.
grammar.n5.08.9.idea: まだ + affirmative: the situation continues.
grammar.n5.08.9.exercise.question: What does the sentence mean?
grammar.n5.08.9.exercise.success: まだ indicates that being at home remains true.
grammar.n5.08.9.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. まだ indicates that being at home remains true.
grammar.n5.08.9.preview: まだあついです。 — It is still hot.
grammar.n5.08.10.title: まだ～ていません
grammar.n5.08.10.goal: Say that an expected action has not happened yet.
grammar.n5.08.10.rule: まだ + て form + いません expresses that you have not yet done an expected action. This differs from negating a habit, as in たべません.
grammar.n5.08.10.example.0: まだたべていません。 — I have not eaten yet.
grammar.n5.08.10.example.1: まだほんをよんでいません。 — I have not read the book yet.
grammar.n5.08.10.idea: まだ + ていません: not completed yet.
grammar.n5.08.10.exercise.success: まだみていません means watching it is still pending, not that you are still watching it.
grammar.n5.08.10.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. まだみていません means watching it is still pending, not that you are still watching it.
grammar.n5.08.10.preview: まだたべていません。 — I have not eaten yet.
grammar.n5.08.11.title: Before: まえに
grammar.n5.08.11.rule: Verb in dictionary form + まえに places the main action before that action. With a noun, use noun + のまえに. The verb before まえに does not take the past form even if the final sentence does.
grammar.n5.08.11.example.0: ねるまえにほんをよみます。 — I read before going to bed.
grammar.n5.08.11.example.1: しょくじのまえにてをあらいます。 — I wash my hands before eating.
grammar.n5.08.11.idea: Dictionary form + まえに: before doing.
grammar.n5.08.11.exercise.success: Before まえに, use the dictionary form ねる; the past appears in のみました.
grammar.n5.08.11.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. Before まえに, use the dictionary form ねる; the past appears in のみました.
grammar.n5.08.11.preview: ねるまえにほんをよみます。 — I read before going to bed.
grammar.n5.08.journey.title: Learn step by step
grammar.n5.08.practice.title: Topic 08 review
grammar.n5.08.practice.body: Mix what you have learned with new examples. Read the whole sentence before choosing; the feedback explains each answer.
grammar.n5.08.practice.0.question: Complete the reason.
grammar.n5.08.practice.0.prompt: さむいです＿、うちにいます。 — Because it is cold, I am at home.
grammar.n5.08.practice.0.success: から introduces the reason for staying at home.
grammar.n5.08.practice.0.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. から introduces the reason for staying at home.
grammar.n5.08.practice.1.question: Complete “Because I am a student, I study every day”.
grammar.n5.08.practice.1.prompt: がくせい＿、まいにちべんきょうします。
grammar.n5.08.practice.1.success: Affirmative non-past nouns connect with なので.
grammar.n5.08.practice.1.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. Affirmative non-past nouns connect with なので.
grammar.n5.08.practice.2.question: Complete the requested contrast.
grammar.n5.08.practice.2.prompt: ちいさいです＿、おもしろいです。 — It is small, but interesting.
grammar.n5.08.practice.2.success: けど connects the contrast in the prompt.
grammar.n5.08.practice.2.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. けど connects the contrast in the prompt.
grammar.n5.08.practice.3.question: What does が after です mean?
grammar.n5.08.practice.3.prompt: このまちはしずかですが、べんりです。
grammar.n5.08.practice.3.success: That が links two contrasting sentences: but.
grammar.n5.08.practice.3.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. That が links two contrasting sentences: but.
grammar.n5.08.practice.4.question: Choose the list presented as complete.
grammar.n5.08.practice.4.prompt: I buy a pen and a notebook.
grammar.n5.08.practice.4.option.0: ペンとノートをかいます。
grammar.n5.08.practice.4.option.1: ペンやノートをかいます。
grammar.n5.08.practice.4.option.2: ペンがノートをかいます。
grammar.n5.08.practice.4.success: と joins both items as a complete list in this context; や would give examples.
grammar.n5.08.practice.4.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. と joins both items as a complete list in this context; や would give examples.
grammar.n5.08.practice.5.question: What does this sentence limit?
grammar.n5.08.practice.5.prompt: コーヒーだけをのみます。
grammar.n5.08.practice.5.success: だけ limits the object to コーヒー.
grammar.n5.08.practice.5.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. だけ limits the object to コーヒー.
grammar.n5.08.practice.7.question: What does the answer imply?
grammar.n5.08.practice.7.prompt: もうしゅくだいをしました。 · しゅくだい = homework
grammar.n5.08.practice.7.success: もう + past indicates that the action is already complete.
grammar.n5.08.practice.7.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. もう + past indicates that the action is already complete.
grammar.n5.08.practice.8.question: Choose “I have not returned home yet”.
grammar.n5.08.practice.8.option.1: まだうちにかえっていません。
grammar.n5.08.practice.8.success: まだ + ていません indicates an action still pending.
grammar.n5.08.practice.8.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. まだ + ていません indicates an action still pending.
grammar.n5.08.practice.9.question: Complete “I read before studying”.
grammar.n5.08.practice.9.success: まえに attaches to the verb in dictionary form, べんきょうする.
grammar.n5.08.practice.9.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. まえに attaches to the verb in dictionary form, べんきょうする.
grammar.n5.09.1.title: たことがある
grammar.n5.09.1.goal: Talk about an experience you have had at some point.
grammar.n5.09.1.rule: た form + ことがあります expresses life experience. It does not just recount an event yesterday; it means you have done something at some point. The exact time is not the main point.
grammar.n5.09.1.example.0: にほんにいったことがあります。 — I have been to Japan before.
grammar.n5.09.1.example.1: すしをたべたことがあります。 — I have tried sushi.
grammar.n5.09.1.idea: た form + ことがある: have done it before.
grammar.n5.09.1.exercise.prompt: このえいがを＿ことがあります。
grammar.n5.09.1.exercise.success: Experience is formed with plain past みた + ことがあります.
grammar.n5.09.1.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. Experience is formed with plain past みた + ことがあります.
grammar.n5.09.1.preview: にほんにいったことがあります。 — I have been to Japan before.
grammar.n5.09.2.title: たことがない
grammar.n5.09.2.goal: Say you have never had an experience.
grammar.n5.09.2.rule: Keep the た form and negate the existence of the experience: ことがありません or ことがない. Do not negate the experience verb.
grammar.n5.09.2.example.0: にほんにいったことがありません。 — I have never been to Japan.
grammar.n5.09.2.example.1: すしをたべたことがない。 — I have never tried sushi.
grammar.n5.09.2.idea: Negation goes in ある → ない / ありません, not inside the た form.
grammar.n5.09.2.exercise.question: Choose “I have never drunk coffee”.
grammar.n5.09.2.exercise.option.0: のまなかったことがあります
grammar.n5.09.2.exercise.option.1: のんだことがありません
grammar.n5.09.2.exercise.option.2: のまないことがあります
grammar.n5.09.2.exercise.success: のんだことがありません denies having the experience of drinking coffee.
grammar.n5.09.2.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. のんだことがありません denies having the experience of drinking coffee.
grammar.n5.09.2.preview: にほんにいったことがありません。 — I have never been to Japan.
grammar.n5.09.3.title: つもり — intention
grammar.n5.09.3.goal: Express what you intend to do.
grammar.n5.09.3.rule: Dictionary form + つもりです expresses an intention. ない form + つもりです expresses an intention not to do something. It is your own plan; it does not guarantee it will happen.
grammar.n5.09.3.example.0: あしたべんきょうするつもりです。 — I intend to study tomorrow.
grammar.n5.09.3.example.1: きょうはいかないつもりです。 — I plan not to go today.
grammar.n5.09.3.idea: Dictionary / ない + つもりです.
grammar.n5.09.3.exercise.prompt: あしたほんを＿つもりです。
grammar.n5.09.3.exercise.success: よむ is the dictionary form used before つもり.
grammar.n5.09.3.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. よむ is the dictionary form used before つもり.
grammar.n5.09.3.preview: あしたべんきょうするつもりです。 — I intend to study tomorrow.
grammar.n5.09.4.title: より・のほうが — comparison
grammar.n5.09.4.goal: Indicate which of two things has more of a quality.
grammar.n5.09.4.rule: A より B のほうが + description presents B as more than A. より introduces the comparison reference. Do not add a separate word for “more” before the adjective.
grammar.n5.09.4.example.0: コーヒーよりおちゃのほうがすきです。 — I like tea more than coffee.
grammar.n5.09.4.example.1: バスよりでんしゃのほうがはやいです。 — The train is faster than the bus.
grammar.n5.09.4.idea: A is the reference; B has more of that quality.
grammar.n5.09.4.exercise.success: ケーキ appears with のほうが: cake is more expensive than bread, the reference marked with より.
grammar.n5.09.4.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. ケーキ appears with のほうが: cake is more expensive than bread, the reference marked with より.
grammar.n5.09.4.preview: コーヒーよりおちゃのほうがすきです。 — I like tea more than coffee.
grammar.n5.09.5.title: のなかで・いちばん
grammar.n5.09.5.goal: Choose the most outstanding item within a group.
grammar.n5.09.5.rule: Group のなかで + item がいちばん + description expresses a superlative within that set. いちばん means the most in that context, not “very” without comparison.
grammar.n5.09.5.example.0: くだもののなかでりんごがいちばんすきです。 — Of all fruits, I like apples best.
grammar.n5.09.5.example.1: このクラスでたなかさんがいちばんせがたかいです。 — Tanaka is the tallest in this class.
grammar.n5.09.5.idea: Define the set, then identify the item with がいちばん.
grammar.n5.09.5.exercise.question: Which is the favourite within the group?
grammar.n5.09.5.exercise.prompt: のみもののなかでみずがいちばんすきです。 · のみもの = drinks
grammar.n5.09.5.exercise.success: みず is the item identified as the favourite by がいちばんすき.
grammar.n5.09.5.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. みず is the item identified as the favourite by がいちばんすき.
grammar.n5.09.5.preview: くだもののなかでりんごがいちばんすきです。 — Of all fruits, I like apples best.
grammar.n5.09.6.title: になる・くなる — change
grammar.n5.09.6.goal: Describe a new state without presenting it as a choice.
grammar.n5.09.6.rule: なる expresses reaching a state. Nouns and な adjectives use に; い adjectives change い to く. The past なりました describes a change that happened.
grammar.n5.09.6.example.0: せんせいになりました。 — I became a teacher.
grammar.n5.09.6.example.1: さむくなりました。 — It got cold.
grammar.n5.09.6.idea: Noun/な adjective + に; い adjective → く + なる.
grammar.n5.09.6.exercise.success: しずか is a な adjective: the change uses に, しずかになりました.
grammar.n5.09.6.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. しずか is a な adjective: the change uses に, しずかになりました.
grammar.n5.09.6.preview: せんせいになりました。 — I became a teacher.
grammar.n5.09.7.title: にする — choice
grammar.n5.09.7.rule: Noun + にします indicates a choice between options. It is common when ordering at a café. It contrasts with になります, which describes a change of state without expressing that decision.
grammar.n5.09.7.example.0: コーヒーにします。 — I'll choose coffee.
grammar.n5.09.7.example.1: このほんにします。 — I'll take this book.
grammar.n5.09.7.idea: Option + にする: choose that option.
grammar.n5.09.7.exercise.question: Choose the answer “I'll take tea”.
grammar.n5.09.7.exercise.success: おちゃにします expresses choosing tea.
grammar.n5.09.7.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. おちゃにします expresses choosing tea.
grammar.n5.09.7.preview: コーヒーにします。 — I'll choose coffee.
grammar.n5.09.8.title: すぎる — too much
grammar.n5.09.8.goal: Indicate that an action or quality exceeds what is appropriate.
grammar.n5.09.8.rule: Verbs: ます stem + すぎる. い adjectives: remove the final い; な adjectives: use the stem without な. すぎます keeps the polite form. For いい, use よすぎる.
grammar.n5.09.8.example.0: たべすぎました。 — I ate too much.
grammar.n5.09.8.example.1: このへやはしずかすぎます。 — This room is too quiet.
grammar.n5.09.8.idea: Verb stem or adjective stem + すぎる.
grammar.n5.09.8.exercise.question: Choose “It is too expensive”.
grammar.n5.09.8.exercise.success: たかい loses its final い before すぎる: たかすぎます.
grammar.n5.09.8.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. たかい loses its final い before すぎる: たかすぎます.
grammar.n5.09.8.preview: たべすぎました。 — I ate too much.
grammar.n5.09.9.title: でしょう・だろう
grammar.n5.09.9.goal: Recognize a supposition without treating it as certainty.
grammar.n5.09.9.rule: でしょう expresses a supposition and can sound polite; だろう is its plain variant, included here for recognition. With verbs and い adjectives, use the plain form; with affirmative non-past nouns and な adjectives, do not add だ before でしょう.
grammar.n5.09.9.example.0: あしたはあめでしょう。 — It will probably rain tomorrow.
grammar.n5.09.9.example.1: たなかさんはくるだろう。 — Tanaka will probably come.
grammar.n5.09.9.idea: Recognize probability; do not confuse a supposition with a certain fact.
grammar.n5.09.9.exercise.question: What does the sentence communicate?
grammar.n5.09.9.exercise.prompt: あしたはさむいでしょう。
grammar.n5.09.9.exercise.option.0: It states without any doubt that it will be cold.
grammar.n5.09.9.exercise.option.2: It will probably be cold tomorrow.
grammar.n5.09.9.exercise.success: でしょう presents a supposition: it will probably be cold.
grammar.n5.09.9.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. でしょう presents a supposition: it will probably be cold.
grammar.n5.09.9.preview: あしたはあめでしょう。 — It will probably rain tomorrow.
grammar.n5.09.10.title: あげる — give to someone else
grammar.n5.09.10.goal: Follow the direction of the object from the giver.
grammar.n5.09.10.rule: With あげる, the giver is the subject; the recipient takes に; the gift takes を. For the initial viewpoint: ME → someone else. It is also used between other people depending on context.
grammar.n5.09.10.example.0: わたし → ともだち：ほんをあげます。 — I give a book to a friend.
grammar.n5.09.10.example.1: あねはともだちにかばんをあげました。 — My sister gave a bag to a friend.
grammar.n5.09.10.idea: Giver は + recipient に + object をあげる. ME → someone else.
grammar.n5.09.10.preview: わたし → ともだち：ほんをあげます。 — I give a book to a friend.
grammar.n5.09.11.title: くれる — give to me
grammar.n5.09.11.goal: Recognize a gift from someone else to you.
grammar.n5.09.11.rule: くれる presents the giver as the subject and the direction towards me or someone on my side. The gift takes を; the recipient can be omitted if clear. ME is not the giver in the basic pattern.
grammar.n5.09.11.example.0: ともだち → わたし：ほんをくれます。 — A friend gives me a book.
grammar.n5.09.11.example.1: たなかさんはわたしにペンをくれました。 — Tanaka gave me a pen.
grammar.n5.09.11.idea: Someone else → ME: giver は + object をくれる.
grammar.n5.09.11.preview: ともだち → わたし：ほんをくれます。 — A friend gives me a book.
grammar.n5.09.12.title: もらう — receive
grammar.n5.09.12.goal: Describe the same exchange from the recipient's perspective.
grammar.n5.09.12.rule: もらう means receive. The recipient is the subject; the person you receive from takes に or から; the object takes を. The subject changes compared to くれる, although the gift may be the same.
grammar.n5.09.12.example.0: わたし ← ともだち：ほんをもらいます。 — I receive a book from a friend.
grammar.n5.09.12.example.1: わたしはあねからかばんをもらいました。 — I received a bag from my sister.
grammar.n5.09.12.idea: Recipient は + giver に / から + object をもらう.
grammar.n5.09.12.preview: わたし ← ともだち：ほんをもらいます。 — I receive a book from a friend.
grammar.n5.09.journey.title: Learn step by step
grammar.n5.09.practice.title: Topic 09 review
grammar.n5.09.practice.body: Mix what you have learned with new examples. Read the whole sentence before choosing; the feedback explains each answer.
grammar.n5.09.practice.0.question: Complete a travel experience.
grammar.n5.09.practice.0.prompt: とうきょうに＿ことがあります。 · いく = to go
grammar.n5.09.practice.0.success: Experience uses the た form: いったことがあります.
grammar.n5.09.practice.0.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. Experience uses the た form: いったことがあります.
grammar.n5.09.practice.1.question: Choose “I have never swum”.
grammar.n5.09.practice.1.option.0: およいだことがありません。
grammar.n5.09.practice.1.option.1: およがなかったことがあります。
grammar.n5.09.practice.1.success: Experience negation goes in ことがありません, keeping およいだ.

grammar.n5.10.1.title: Mixed particles
grammar.n5.10.1.goal: Choose particles by their function within a complete sentence.
grammar.n5.10.1.rule: Do not translate a particle in isolation. は introduces the topic; が marks what is described or exists; に marks destination, time or existence; で action; を object; へ direction; と company; の relation; も also; から origin or reason; まで limit.
grammar.n5.10.1.example.0: わたしはうちでほんをよみます。 — I read a book at home.
grammar.n5.10.1.example.1: くじからごじまで、がっこうでべんきょうします。 — I study at school from nine to five.
grammar.n5.10.1.idea: Find the verb and ask what function each noun has.
grammar.n5.10.1.preview: わたしはうちでほんをよみます。 — I read a book at home.
grammar.n5.10.2.title: Mixed conjugations
grammar.n5.10.2.goal: Keep tense and negation when changing politeness.
grammar.n5.10.2.rule: Identify three things: politeness, tense and affirmation or negation. Rebuild the form using the verb group. The て form connects; the last verb usually determines tense and politeness.
grammar.n5.10.2.example.0: たべませんでした ↔ たべなかった — I did not eat.
grammar.n5.10.2.example.1: よんで、ねました。 — I read and went to bed.
grammar.n5.10.2.idea: Do not lose negation or past tense when changing register.
grammar.n5.10.2.preview: たべませんでした ↔ たべなかった — I did not eat.
grammar.n5.10.3.title: Form selection
grammar.n5.10.3.goal: Fill a gap using the surrounding structure.
grammar.n5.10.3.rule: Read before and after the gap. Expressions like まえに require dictionary form; ことがある requires た; ください for an affirmative request requires て. General meaning is not enough: check the connection.
grammar.n5.10.3.example.0: ねるまえに、みずをのみます。 — I drink water before sleeping.
grammar.n5.10.3.example.1: にほんにいったことがあります。 — I have been to Japan.
grammar.n5.10.3.idea: First recognize the pattern; then build the required form.
grammar.n5.10.3.exercise.question: Select the appropriate form for a request.
grammar.n5.10.3.exercise.prompt: ここに＿ください。 · すわる = sit down
grammar.n5.10.3.exercise.success: An affirmative request uses て form + ください: すわってください.
grammar.n5.10.3.exercise.error: Review the relationship between form and meaning. An affirmative request uses て form + ください: すわってください.
grammar.n5.10.3.preview: ねるまえに、みずをのみます。 — I drink water before sleeping.
grammar.n5.10.4.title: Sentence order
grammar.n5.10.4.goal: Order blocks without splitting a grammatical unit.
grammar.n5.10.4.rule: The predicate usually goes last. Each noun stays with its particle; a description goes before the noun. Here you practise composition with options using the engine you already know.
grammar.n5.10.4.example.0: わたしは / このほんを / よみたいです。 — I want to read this book.
grammar.n5.10.4.example.1: きのうみた / えいがは / おもしろかったです。 — The film I watched yesterday was interesting.
grammar.n5.10.4.idea: Keep each particle with its noun and the description before what it describes.
grammar.n5.10.4.preview: わたしは / このほんを / よみたいです。 — I want to read this book.
grammar.n5.10.5.title: Grammar within text
grammar.n5.10.5.goal: Use context to connect two sentences coherently.
grammar.n5.10.5.rule: A gap may depend on the meaning of the entire text. Decide whether the second idea gives a consequence, a contrast or a continuation. Do not choose only because an ending fits grammatically.
grammar.n5.10.5.example.0: このみせはたかいですけど、おいしいです。 — This shop is expensive, but its food is tasty.
grammar.n5.10.5.example.1: あめがふっていますから、うちにいます。 — Because it is raining, I am at home.
grammar.n5.10.5.idea: Relate the ideas before choosing the connector.
grammar.n5.10.5.preview: このみせはたかいですけど、おいしいです。 — This shop is expensive, but its food is tasty.
grammar.n5.10.6.title: Short reading
grammar.n5.10.6.goal: Extract a specific action from a short text.
grammar.n5.10.6.rule: Read the whole text once. Then find what the question asks for: person, place, time or action. You do not need to translate word for word to locate that information.
grammar.n5.10.6.example.0: きょうはにちようびです。わたしはうちでほんをよみます。 — Today is Sunday. I read at home.
grammar.n5.10.6.example.1: あしたはがっこうにいきます。 — Tomorrow I am going to school.
grammar.n5.10.6.idea: Find the requested information in the text; do not invent it from a single word.
grammar.n5.10.6.preview: きょうはにちようびです。わたしはうちでほんをよみます。 — Today is Sunday. I read at home.
grammar.n5.10.7.title: Medium reading
grammar.n5.10.7.goal: Relate several times without mixing up the plans.
grammar.n5.10.7.rule: In a longer text, mentally mark expressions like きのう, きょう and あした. Follow the subjects and the order indicated by てから or まえに. Answer only with information from the text.
grammar.n5.10.7.example.0: きのうはやすみでした。うちでほんをよんで、はやくねました。 — Yesterday was a day off. I read at home and went to bed early.
grammar.n5.10.7.example.1: きょうはがっこうにいきます。べんきょうしてから、かえります。 — Today I am going to school. I return after studying.
grammar.n5.10.7.idea: Separate the time references and preserve the order of actions.
grammar.n5.10.7.preview: きのうはやすみでした。うちでほんをよんで、はやくねました。 — Yesterday was a day off. I read at home and went to bed early.
grammar.n5.10.8.title: Practical information
grammar.n5.10.8.goal: Read schedules and notices to decide what you can do.
grammar.n5.10.8.rule: First find useful information: opening, closing, permission or prohibition. から and まで delimit the schedule; てはいけません prohibits; てもいい permits. Do not add assumptions the notice does not state.
grammar.n5.10.8.example.0: としょかん：くじからごじまで。 — Library: nine to five.
grammar.n5.10.8.example.1: ここでたべてはいけません。 — Eating is not allowed here.
grammar.n5.10.8.idea: Connect the notice's time or rule with the question's situation.
grammar.n5.10.8.preview: としょかん：くじからごじまで。 — Library: nine to five.
grammar.n5.10.9.title: Reviewing mistakes
grammar.n5.10.9.goal: Classify a mistake to review the right idea.
grammar.n5.10.9.rule: When correcting, distinguish a particle, conjugation or connection problem. Explain with a specific rule why you would change the form. This page teaches the method; it does not save an error history.
grammar.n5.10.9.example.0: うちにべんきょうします → うちでべんきょうします。 — The location of an action takes で.
grammar.n5.10.9.example.1: たかいでした → たかかったです。 — The い adjective forms its past within the word.
grammar.n5.10.9.preview: うちにべんきょうします → うちでべんきょうします。 — The location of an action takes で.
grammar.n5.10.10.title: N5 mock test
grammar.n5.10.10.goal: Combine form, context and comprehension in a short review.
grammar.n5.10.10.rule: This V1 offers representative questions, not a complete official exam. Before answering, identify the task: complete a form, choose an order or understand a text. Use cumulative practice to combine these decisions.
grammar.n5.10.10.example.0: もうたべました。 — I have already eaten.
grammar.n5.10.10.example.1: まだたべていません。 — I have not eaten yet.
grammar.n5.10.10.idea: Read the instructions, check the pattern and compare your answer with the context.
grammar.n5.10.10.preview: もうたべました。 — I have already eaten.

grammar.audit.01.1.rule: Topic → information → ending is a useful introductory pattern for nominal sentences. It is not a universal rule: the topic is omitted if already known and order can vary with context.
grammar.audit.01.1.idea: Practise this pattern as a starting point. Not all sentences need an explicit topic or follow a single order.
grammar.audit.lesson.01.1.question: Order this introductory nominal sentence.
grammar.audit.lesson.01.1.prompt: Start with これ and end with the polite ending: “This is a book”.
grammar.audit.lesson.01.1.success: これはほんです. This is a useful initial pattern; the topic may be omitted or the order vary when context allows.
grammar.audit.lesson.01.1.error: これはほんです. This is a useful initial pattern; the topic may be omitted or the order vary when context allows.

grammar.audit.lesson.01.7.error: ゆきさんのかばんです: の connects Yuki with her bag.

grammar.audit.theory.04.11:
A: いついきますか。 — When are you going?
B: ごがつふつかにいきます。 — I am going on May 2.
A: みっかはどうですか。 — How about the 3rd?
Learn the date within an appointment: ふつか (day 2), みっか (day 3). The exercise and practice use this distinction again.
grammar.audit.theory.04.11.title: Dates for a plan
grammar.audit.theory.05.8:
A: どうしておくれましたか。 — Why were you late?
B: でんしゃがおそかったんです。 — The train was late, you see.
んです provides the explanation connecting to the question. It does not add a new cause by itself. おくれる = be late; でんしゃ = train; おそい = late/slow.
grammar.audit.theory.05.8.title: An explanation in dialogue

manga.guide.title: Your first read in Japanese
manga.guide.intro: Read first. Look things up when you need to.
manga.guide.text1: Import a ZIP or CBZ containing images and one .mokuro file (version 0.2 or later). Images must match the OCR. You can also use a supported Mokuro import link. Use content you have permission to read.
manga.guide.text2: Mokuro text overlays the image. You can select it, tap it and show it from reading settings. Both vertical and horizontal panels work.
manga.guide.text3: JMdict shows readings and Spanish meanings. The lookup tries to recover the base form of conjugated verbs and adjectives. Ambiguous forms may have alternatives; a lookup does not replace context.
manga.guide.text4: Translate looks for a natural meaning in the context of the sentence. It is a voluntary action requiring the configured contextual service and a connection. Opening a page never translates it automatically.
manga.guide.text5: Try reading first. Look things up only when needed. Close the help to return to the story; adjust zoom and continue from your last saved page.
manga.guide.q1: Is my manga uploaded to a server?
manga.guide.a1: Import and reading store images and OCR in this browser without uploading them. Remote import downloads files and may use the Mokuro relay. If contextual help is configured and requested, only limited OCR text is sent to the chosen service, never images or the whole volume.
manga.guide.a2: Imported manga and the installed dictionary can be used locally while the app is open. Reopening the website offline is not guaranteed. Downloading files, installing or updating JMdict and requesting new contextual help require a connection.
manga.guide.a3: Mokuro generates OCR containing Japanese text and its positions on images. Kana Study reads that file; it does not run OCR on unprepared images.
manga.guide.a4: JMdict is installed once in the browser to look up words without sending queries to a server. It is shared across workspaces and an unsuccessful update preserves the previous installation.
manga.guide.a5: No. It is requested only when you press Translate, if a service is configured. The local dictionary works independently.

grammar.v2.prerequisite: To study grammar, you need to be able to read basic hiragana and katakana.
grammar.v2.reminder: Three readings you will encounter in particles
grammar.v2.waReading: は is pronounced わ when used as a particle.
grammar.v2.heReading: へ is pronounced え when used as a particle.
grammar.v2.woReading: を is usually pronounced お as a particle.
grammar.v2.start: I can read kana → Start Topic 01
grammar.v2.optional: You can continue without taking a test. Return to kana practice whenever you need it.
grammar.v2.topicGoal: Understand context, state what things are and connect ideas with particles.
grammar.v2.reviewBody: Combine nominal forms, particles and demonstrative families in new contexts.
grammar.v2.reviewHelp: Distinguish the intended meaning from grammatical validity. Two valid sentences may answer different questions.
grammar.v2.identified: You have correctly identified the error.
grammar.v2.choose: Choose the answer for this situation.
grammar.v2.order: Arrange the blocks to express the idea.
grammar.v2.match: Match each form to its function.

grammar.v2.speaker: Near me
grammar.v2.question: Question
grammar.v2.sentence-structure-context.su: Context supplies what we already know. The predicate usually closes the sentence; avoid word-for-word translation.
grammar.v2.sentence-structure-context.go: Interpret a short answer without requiring an explicit subject.
grammar.v2.sentence-structure-context.id: Context supplies what we already know. The predicate usually closes the sentence; avoid word-for-word translation.
grammar.v2.sentence-structure-context.ex: A student? → A student. Context tells us who is meant.
grammar.v2.sentence-structure-context.de: A conversation does not restart with each sentence. If both speakers know who they mean, 学生だ is enough to state that the person is a student. The sentence itself does not specify I, you or he.

Leaving out known information does not mean dropping words at random. If the person changes or ambiguity arises, provide more information. This block first examines sentence endings, then how to introduce a topic.
grammar.v2.state-being-plain.title: だ — State what something is
grammar.v2.state-being-plain.summary: だ can close a statement with a noun or a な-adjective. It is not an obligatory equivalent of “be”.
grammar.v2.state-being-plain.goal: Build simple nominal statements and recognise where だ does not fit.
grammar.v2.state-being-plain.idea: だ can close a statement with a noun or a な-adjective. It is not an obligatory equivalent of “be”.
grammar.v2.state-being-plain.detail.0: 学生 names a category; だ makes the assertion explicit. In casual conversation, 学生。 can also be a complete answer when context is sufficient. Do not add だ simply because your translation contains “be”.
grammar.v2.state-being-plain.detail.1: 元気 and 静か belong to the な group. かわいい belongs to the い group and does not take this final だ. Adjectives come in Topic 02. 学生です is valid, but です has its own uses: do not attach it to だ or treat it as a universal replacement. Polite forms come in Topic 05.
grammar.v2.state-being-plain.mistake.0: The い-adjective can already close this sentence.
grammar.v2.state-being-plain.mistake.1: Do not stack だ and です. Here we practise a plain statement.
grammar.v2.state-being-negative.title: じゃない — Say what something is not
grammar.v2.state-being-negative.summary: To negate, follow the noun with じゃない. Do not keep だ before it.
grammar.v2.state-being-negative.goal: Negate a category or nominal state.
grammar.v2.state-being-negative.idea: To negate, follow the noun with じゃない. Do not keep だ before it.
grammar.v2.state-being-negative.detail.0: Negation changes what you assert, not who you are talking about. 学生だ and 学生じゃない can refer to the same person but do not say the same thing.
grammar.v2.state-being-negative.detail.1: If someone assumes you are a student and you are not, 学生じゃない corrects that assumption. 元気 follows the same pattern because it belongs to the な group. Do not automatically extend this form to all adjectives or verbs.
じゃない replaces the affirmative ending; it is not added after だ.
grammar.v2.state-being-negative.contrast: Affirming and denying the same category.
grammar.v2.state-being-past.title: だった — Say what something was
grammar.v2.state-being-past.summary: だった presents a state as past. The small っ is part of the ending.
grammar.v2.state-being-past.goal: Place a nominal statement in the past.
grammar.v2.state-being-past.idea: だった presents a state as past. The small っ is part of the ending.
grammar.v2.state-being-past.detail.0: With 学生だった you place the description in an earlier period. There is no need to add another word meaning “was”: the ending already supplies the tense.
grammar.v2.state-being-past.detail.1: Talking about the past does not by itself establish the situation now. Context can clarify it. Write だった with small っ: だた is not this form.
grammar.v2.state-being-past.mistake.0: The small っ in だった is missing.
grammar.v2.state-being-past-negative.tit: じゃなかった — Say what something was not
grammar.v2.state-being-past-negative.sum: じゃない becomes じゃなかった. Time and negation are two choices you can combine.
grammar.v2.state-being-past-negative.goa: Combine past tense and negation without confusing them.
grammar.v2.state-being-past-negative.ide: じゃない becomes じゃなかった. Time and negation are two choices you can combine.
grammar.v2.state-being-past-negative.det: First decide whether you affirm or negate, then place the state in time. To negate a past state, replace the final い of じゃない with かった. Do not join だった and じゃない.

All four forms in the table are valid Japanese. Choosing the wrong one for a situation changes the meaning; it does not automatically make the sentence ungrammatical. “Non-past” includes present uses and others determined by context.
grammar.v2.particle-wa-topic.title: は — What we are talking about
grammar.v2.particle-wa-topic.summary: は marks the topic we give information about. As a particle it is read わ.
grammar.v2.particle-wa-topic.goal: Introduce a topic and distinguish it from the information about it.
grammar.v2.particle-wa-topic.idea: は marks the topic we give information about. As a particle it is read わ.
grammar.v2.particle-wa-topic.example.0: As for Tanaka, they are a student.
grammar.v2.particle-wa-topic.example.1: Is Tanaka a student? → A student, yes; the topic need not be repeated.
grammar.v2.particle-wa-topic.detail.0: Think of は as the frame for the information that follows. In 田中さんは学生だ, 田中さん is the topic and 学生だ is what we communicate about them. は does not mean “be”.
grammar.v2.particle-wa-topic.detail.1: Topic and subject are not interchangeable labels in every sentence. This example may seem easy to translate, but は organises what we talk about. Once the topic is established, an answer can leave it out.
grammar.v2.particle-mo-inclusive.title: も — Also
grammar.v2.particle-mo-inclusive.summary: も includes another item in an established statement. In this pattern it takes the place of は.
grammar.v2.particle-mo-inclusive.goal: Add another item to which the same information applies.
grammar.v2.particle-mo-inclusive.idea: も includes another item in an established statement. In this pattern it takes the place of は.
grammar.v2.particle-mo-inclusive.example: Tanaka is a student. Yamada is too.
“Also” needs something to match. In the example, both people are students. If you only want to introduce Yamada without adding them to shared information, も does not express that intention.
A negative statement can be shared too: 田中さんも学生じゃない adds Tanaka to those who are not students. The relevant information must match; repeating a word is not enough.
grammar.v2.particle-mo-inclusive.mistake: In this pattern も replaces は; they do not stack.
grammar.v2.particle-ga-identifier.title: が — Identify who or what
grammar.v2.particle-ga-identifier.summar: が helps identify the item that fits the description. 誰 means “who”.
grammar.v2.particle-ga-identifier.goal: Answer a question of identity using が.
grammar.v2.particle-ga-identifier.idea: が helps identify the item that fits the description. 誰 means “who”.
grammar.v2.particle-ga-identifier.exampl: Who is a teacher? → Yamada is the one.
grammar.v2.particle-ga-identifier.detail: In 誰が学生？ we are still looking for the person. The answer 田中さんが学生だ fills that identity slot with Tanaka. We do not need a fixed word-for-word translation of が to understand its role.

This is a first use of が, not an exhaustive definition. Later you will encounter it with existence, preferences and ability. Memorising only “が = subject” does not explain why we choose it in this dialogue.
grammar.v2.particle-wa-vs-ga.title: は and が — Topic versus identification
grammar.v2.particle-wa-vs-ga.summary: は → “as for…”. が → “the one / thing that…”. This is an initial model, not a literal translation.
grammar.v2.particle-wa-vs-ga.goal: Choose according to what information the sentence adds to the dialogue.
grammar.v2.particle-wa-vs-ga.idea: は → “as for…”. が → “the one / thing that…”. This is an initial model, not a literal translation.
grammar.v2.particle-wa-vs-ga.example.0: About Tanaka, we give the information that they are a student.
grammar.v2.particle-wa-vs-ga.example.1: We ask who; we identify Tanaka.
grammar.v2.particle-wa-vs-ga.detail.0: With は we start from a topic and say something about it. In the use of が practised here, we identify who fits a description. Context determines what information needs highlighting.
grammar.v2.particle-wa-vs-ga.detail.1: 田中さんは学生だ and 田中さんが学生だ are both valid sentences. Do not turn a contextual preference into a universal ban. Exercises specify whether we introduce a topic or identify someone; finer distinctions come later.
grammar.v2.particle-wa-vs-ga.contrast.0: Same person and category; the information is organised differently.
grammar.v2.particle-no-noun-link.title: の — Connect nouns
grammar.v2.particle-no-noun-link.summary: In A の B, A specifies or relates to B. B is the head; the relationship is not always ownership.
grammar.v2.particle-no-noun-link.goal: Recognise the head noun and the noun that specifies it.
grammar.v2.particle-no-noun-link.idea: In A の B, A specifies or relates to B. B is the head; the relationship is not always ownership.
Start at the end: 日本語の先生 refers to a teacher, and 日本語 specifies their subject. It does not mean the language owns the person. With ゆきさんの本, the relationship can be ownership.
Changing the order changes the head. The modifying phrase comes before the main noun, even if your translation puts it after. Here we study only の between nouns; other uses come later.
grammar.v2.demonstratives-ko-so-a-do.tit: こ・そ・あ・ど — Point to things and places
grammar.v2.demonstratives-ko-so-a-do.sum: First choose こ・そ・あ・ど; then decide whether you point to a thing, accompany a noun or indicate a place.
grammar.v2.demonstratives-ko-so-a-do.goa: Combine distance or context with the family the sentence needs.
grammar.v2.demonstratives-ko-so-a-do.ide: First choose こ・そ・あ・ど; then decide whether you point to a thing, accompany a noun or indicate a place.

grammar.v2.adjective-na.title: な-adjectives: the bridge from nouns
grammar.v2.adjective-na.summary: 静か behaves like 学生 when ending a statement: 静かだ, 静かじゃない, 静かだった, 静かじゃなかった.
grammar.v2.adjective-na.goal: Recognise the な group and reuse the nominal forms from Topic 01.
grammar.v2.adjective-na.idea: 静か behaves like 学生 when ending a statement: 静かだ, 静かじゃない, 静かだった, 静かじゃなかった.
grammar.v2.adjective-na.detail.0: You already know 学生だ and its three variants. The な group shares that predicate system: keep 静か and choose the ending for tense and negation. You do not need four new mechanisms.
grammar.v2.adjective-na.detail.1: Learn the group with the word. きれい and 嫌い（きらい） end in い but belong to the な group. That letter alone cannot classify them. な links the adjective to a following noun; it does not stay before だ. We will compare both groups when describing nouns.
grammar.v2.adjective-na.contrast.0: The same ending negates a past state.
grammar.v2.adjective-i.title: い-adjectives: a complete description
grammar.v2.adjective-i.summary: 高い, 面白い and かわいい can be predicates on their own. Their final い participates in conjugation.
grammar.v2.adjective-i.goal: End a description with an い-adjective without adding だ.
grammar.v2.adjective-i.idea: 高い, 面白い and かわいい can be predicates on their own. Their final い participates in conjugation.
grammar.v2.adjective-i.example.0: It is expensive / tall, depending on context.
grammar.v2.adjective-i.detail.0: These predicates are not missing a word meaning “be”. 高い already describes a quality. Unlike 静かだ, we do not add だ after it. Later we will change its last い to negate or talk about the past.
grammar.v2.adjective-i.detail.1: Spelling helps but does not determine the group on its own: きれい and 嫌い are な. In かわいい there are two consecutive い; the last one is the ending that changes. Learn the dictionary form and group together.
grammar.v2.adjective-i.mistake.0: 高い already works as a predicate; it does not take that だ.
grammar.v2.adjective-i.mistake.1: Do not add だ to an い-group predicate.
grammar.v2.adjective-noun-modification.t: Describing a noun: い or な
grammar.v2.adjective-noun-modification.s: The い group goes directly before a noun. The な group uses な there: 高い本, 静かな町.
grammar.v2.adjective-noun-modification.g: Build adjective–noun phrases with the appropriate link.
grammar.v2.adjective-noun-modification.i: The い group goes directly before a noun. The な group uses な there: 高い本, 静かな町.
grammar.v2.adjective-noun-modification.d: Compare 部屋は静かだ。 with 静かな部屋. In the first sentence you state what the room is like; in the second you describe which room. な is not permanently attached to the adjective: it appears as a link before the noun in this construction.
The noun comes last in the phrase. 大きい家 is about a house, and 大きい gives its size. Do not insert な after an い-adjective or omit the link in 静かな町. Here we practise non-past affirmative descriptions.
grammar.v2.adjective-noun-modification.m: The い group joins directly to the noun.
The link な is missing before the noun.
grammar.v2.adjective-negative.title: Negating a quality
grammar.v2.adjective-negative.summary: な reuses nominal negation: 静かじゃない. For い, replace the final い with くない: 高くない.
grammar.v2.adjective-negative.goal: Choose between じゃない and くない according to the group.
grammar.v2.adjective-negative.idea: な reuses nominal negation: 静かじゃない. For い, replace the final い with くない: 高くない.
grammar.v2.adjective-negative.detail.0: Decide the group first. 静か keeps its base and changes the nominal ending. 高い changes internally: 高 + くない. The removed い does not remain before くない; 高いくない is not the negative form.
grammar.v2.adjective-negative.detail.1: Denying “expensive” does not necessarily mean “cheap”: the price may be ordinary. We practise the plain descriptive negative 高くない. Do not confuse this goal with other conversational uses of じゃない found in real Japanese.
grammar.v2.adjective-negative.mistake.0: Replace the final い; do not add くない after it.
grammar.v2.adjective-past.title: Describing the past
grammar.v2.adjective-past.summary: な keeps the nominal system: 静かだった. For い, replace the final い with かった: 高かった.
grammar.v2.adjective-past.goal: Describe an earlier quality with だった or かった.
grammar.v2.adjective-past.idea: な keeps the nominal system: 静かだった. For い, replace the final い with かった: 高かった.
grammar.v2.adjective-past.detail.0: For 高い, separate 高 from the final い and add かった. Do not add the nominal past to the whole word: 高いだった mixes two systems. Small っ is part of both かった and だった.
grammar.v2.adjective-past.detail.1: 昨日 places the example yesterday, but the predicate ending expresses the past. A past description does not by itself prove what the situation is now. We continue using plain forms here.
grammar.v2.adjective-past.mistake.0: The い group changes its ending; it does not use だった after the complete form.
grammar.v2.adjective-past-negative.title: Tense and negation: one system
grammar.v2.adjective-past-negative.summa: To negate in the past: 静かじゃなかった for な, 高くなかった for い. Combine the two choices you already know.
grammar.v2.adjective-past-negative.goal: Choose a form by group, tense and polarity.
grammar.v2.adjective-past-negative.idea: To negate in the past: 静かじゃなかった for な, 高くなかった for い. Combine the two choices you already know.
grammar.v2.adjective-past-negative.examp: Yesterday the town was not quiet.
grammar.v2.adjective-past-negative.detai: Do not memorise eight isolated sentences. The group determines the family of forms; then choose a tense row and an affirmative or negative column. In 高くない, the last い of ない changes to かった to give 高くなかった.
静かだった and 静かじゃなかった are both valid forms, but only one means “was not quiet”. Choosing the wrong tense or polarity changes the meaning: it does not make the other option impossible Japanese.
grammar.v2.adjective-ii-irregular.title: いい: conjugate from よい
grammar.v2.adjective-ii-irregular.summar: いい means “good”. Its conjugated forms start from よい: よくない, よかった, よくなかった.
grammar.v2.adjective-ii-irregular.goal: Use よくない, よかった and よくなかった.
grammar.v2.adjective-ii-irregular.idea: いい means “good”. Its conjugated forms start from よい: よくない, よかった, よくなかった.
grammar.v2.adjective-ii-irregular.detail: You do not get these forms by removing the last い from いい. Recover よい and apply the い-group system: よ + くない, よ + かった, よ + くなかった. This keeps one rule for endings and one special base to remember.
The same alternation appears in かっこいい: かっこよくない and かっこよかった. This extends the pattern rather than creating a new group. いくない and いかった are not conjugations of いい.
grammar.v2.adjective-ii-irregular.mistak: The negative starts from よい.
The past also uses the よ- base.
grammar.v2.degree-adverbs.title: Expressing degree
grammar.v2.degree-adverbs.summary: とても intensifies. あまり with a negative means “not very”. In the basic N5 pattern, ぜんぜん with a negative means “not at all”.
grammar.v2.degree-adverbs.goal: Distinguish very, not very and not at all in basic descriptions.
grammar.v2.degree-adverbs.idea: とても intensifies. あまり with a negative means “not very”. In the basic N5 pattern, ぜんぜん with a negative means “not at all”.
grammar.v2.degree-adverbs.example.2: It is not expensive at all.
grammar.v2.degree-adverbs.detail.0: The degree word goes before the description and changes its intensity. あまり高くない leaves room for some degree; ぜんぜん高くない strongly denies “expensive”. The negative ending is still needed in the patterns we practise.
grammar.v2.degree-adverbs.detail.1: In contemporary casual Japanese you can also encounter ぜんぜん with affirmative expressions. There is no universal ban: here we focus on the basic N5 negative pattern. These words can also modify な descriptions, such as とても静かだ.
grammar.v2.adjectival-predicates-ga.summ: 好き・嫌い express preference; 上手・下手, skill. They belong to the な group. In person は + thing/activity が + predicate, が marks what is being described.
grammar.v2.adjectival-predicates-ga.goal: Describe preferences and skills with な predicates and distinguish は from が in this pattern.
grammar.v2.adjectival-predicates-ga.idea: 好き・嫌い express preference; 上手・下手, skill. They belong to the な group. In person は + thing/activity が + predicate, が marks what is being described.
grammar.v2.adjectival-predicates-ga.deta: Connect this to Topic 01: は introduces the person as the topic; が marks here the thing or activity the description applies to. 好き is not a word-for-word verb equivalent of “like”. 私は魚が好きだ describes fish as something I like; we do not use を for that role in this pattern.

Preference and skill are different: you may like cooking even if you are bad at it. 嫌い ends in い but is な: 嫌いだ, 嫌いじゃない. Using 上手 about yourself may sound self-praising depending on context, but it is not grammatically forbidden. This use of が is not a universal formula for all preferences, verbs or situations.
grammar.v2.adjectival-predicates-ga.mist: In this statement with 好きだ, fish is marked with が, not を.

grammar.v2.topic03Goal: Recognise verb families and combine affirmation, negation and tense in plain forms.
grammar.v2.review03Body: Decide the group, interpret the context and build the plain form you need.
grammar.v2.verb-role-dictionary.title: The verb and dictionary form
grammar.v2.verb-role-dictionary.summary: The verb usually ends the unit and does not change for I, you or he. The dictionary form is non-past affirmative: it can express a habit or the future.
grammar.v2.verb-role-dictionary.goal: Interpret the verb through context without changing it for person.
grammar.v2.verb-role-dictionary.idea: The verb usually ends the unit and does not change for I, you or he. The dictionary form is non-past affirmative: it can express a habit or the future.
I go / will go, depending on context.
Tanaka goes / will go, depending on context.
Eat / will eat; the person and time depend on context.
grammar.v2.verb-role-dictionary.detail.0: Looking up 読む in a dictionary gives a form of the verb read, not a fixed translation “I read”. The ending does not encode first, second or third person. 私は and 田中さんは change the topic, but 行く stays the same.
grammar.v2.verb-role-dictionary.detail.1: 毎日 indicates repetition; 明日 places the action tomorrow. Both take the same 読む form: no separate future ending is needed. As in Topic 01, 食べる can be a sufficient answer when who eats and when are understood. The dictionary form does not by itself express an action in progress.
grammar.v2.verb-ichidan.title: Ichidan: keep the base
grammar.v2.verb-ichidan.summary: In an ichidan such as 食べる, the final る is replaced in conjugation. Many end in いる or える sounds, but this is a clue, not an absolute rule.
grammar.v2.verb-ichidan.goal: Recognise the ichidan family and the part left after removing る.
grammar.v2.verb-ichidan.idea: In an ichidan such as 食べる, the final る is replaced in conjugation. Many end in いる or える sounds, but this is a clue, not an absolute rule.
grammar.v2.verb-ichidan.detail.0: 食べ is the stable part of 食べる in the forms we will learn in this topic. The dots in 食べ… are a visual aid: that base is not a sentence or complete dictionary form here. Later we will add the ending for each conjugation.
grammar.v2.verb-ichidan.detail.1: Learn the group with the verb. 帰る（かえる）, return, is godan even though it sounds as if it ends in える. You therefore cannot always decide from the last two syllables or remove る from every verb ending that way.
grammar.v2.verb-ichidan.contrast.0: The る ending does not identify the group on its own.
grammar.v2.verb-godan.title: Godan: the last kana changes
grammar.v2.verb-godan.summary: Godan verbs end in う・く・ぐ・す・つ・ぬ・ぶ・む・る. The last kana changes row with conjugation; る can also be godan.
grammar.v2.verb-godan.goal: Recognise godan endings and contrast them with ichidan.
grammar.v2.verb-godan.idea: Godan verbs end in う・く・ぐ・す・つ・ぬ・ぶ・む・る. The last kana changes row with conjugation; る can also be godan.
grammar.v2.verb-godan.detail.0: In 書く the 書 part stays while く changes with the form. You are not looking for a single base for all conjugations. First recognise the family and dictionary ending, then apply the change required by the form.
grammar.v2.verb-godan.detail.1: 帰る is the central contrast with 食べる. Other godan ending in る include 入る（はいる）, enter; 走る（はしる）, run; and 切る（きる）, cut. These illustrate why the group must be learned, rather than a list to memorise in full now.
grammar.v2.verb-godan.contrast.0: Both end in る, but belong to different families.
grammar.v2.verb-irregular-suru-kuru.titl: する・来る: two basic irregulars
grammar.v2.verb-irregular-suru-kuru.summ: する means do and 来る（くる） means come. They are the two basic irregulars: we will see their forms when learning each conjugation.
grammar.v2.verb-irregular-suru-kuru.goal: Recognise する, 来る and noun + する combinations.
grammar.v2.verb-irregular-suru-kuru.idea: する means do and 来る（くる） means come. They are the two basic irregulars: we will see their forms when learning each conjugation.
grammar.v2.verb-irregular-suru-kuru.deta: In 勉強する, the activity noun 勉強 combines with する to form a verb. This also happens with 運動 and 電話. Not every noun automatically allows this combination: learn these words as units.

Do not classify する or 来る as ichidan just because they end in る. Their changes do not come from simply applying the regular rule. For now recognise the two families; their negative and past forms will appear in their own lessons.
grammar.v2.verb-negative-plain.title: ない form — not doing something
grammar.v2.verb-negative-plain.summary: Ichidan: replace る with ない. Godan: change the last kana to the あ row and add ない; final う changes to わ. する → しない; 来る → こない.
grammar.v2.verb-negative-plain.goal: Negate an action using the change for its family.
grammar.v2.verb-negative-plain.idea: Ichidan: replace る with ない. Godan: change the last kana to the あ row and add ない; final う changes to わ. する → しない; 来る → こない.
grammar.v2.verb-negative-plain.example.0: I do not eat / will not eat, depending on context.
grammar.v2.verb-negative-plain.example.1: I do not drink / will not drink.
grammar.v2.verb-negative-plain.example.2: I do not do it / will not do it.
grammar.v2.verb-negative-plain.example.3: Does not come / will not come.
grammar.v2.verb-negative-plain.detail.0: The group determines the operation: 食べる loses る and takes ない; 飲む keeps 飲 and changes む to ま before ない. 帰る takes 帰らない because it is godan. The plain negative is still non-past: context distinguishes habit and future.
grammar.v2.verb-negative-plain.detail.1: For final う, remember わ: 買わない, never 買あない. 来る also changes its reading: くる → こない. As a note for Topic 04, the existence negative of ある is ない; we do not assess or develop that use here.
grammar.v2.verb-negative-plain.mistake.0: Final う becomes わ, not あ.
grammar.v2.verb-negative-plain.mistake.1: 食べる is ichidan: replace る without adding ら.
grammar.v2.verb-negative-plain.mistake.2: む changes to ま before ない.
grammar.v2.verb-past-plain.title: た form — past actions
grammar.v2.verb-past-plain.summary: Ichidan: る → た. Godan groups endings: う・つ・る → った; む・ぶ・ぬ → んだ; く → いた; ぐ → いだ; す → した. 行く uses 行った.
grammar.v2.verb-past-plain.goal: Build the plain past using ending families.
grammar.v2.verb-past-plain.idea: Ichidan: る → た. Godan groups endings: う・つ・る → った; む・ぶ・ぬ → んだ; く → いた; ぐ → いだ; す → した. 行く uses 行った.
grammar.v2.verb-past-plain.example.3: Did it; context identifies the person.
grammar.v2.verb-past-plain.detail.0: Identify the group first: 食べる is ichidan, while 帰る is godan and gives 帰った. Within godan recognise one of five families; there is no separate rule to memorise for every verb. Keep the small っ and distinguish た from だ.
grammar.v2.verb-past-plain.detail.1: The exception 行く → 行った does not change the 書く → 書いた rule. The irregulars are する → した and 来る → きた, with the き reading. These sound families will be useful again when studying the て form in another topic; for now we only build the past.
grammar.v2.verb-past-plain.mistake.0: 行く is the important exception to final く.
grammar.v2.verb-past-negative-plain.titl: なかった form — not having done something
grammar.v2.verb-past-negative-plain.summ: First build ない, then replace ない with なかった: 飲む → 飲まない → 飲まなかった.
grammar.v2.verb-past-negative-plain.goal: Start from the negative and place it in the past.
grammar.v2.verb-past-negative-plain.idea: First build ない, then replace ない with なかった: 飲む → 飲まない → 飲まなかった.
grammar.v2.verb-past-negative-plain.deta: You already know the same operation from Topic 02: 高くない → 高くなかった. Do not look up the affirmative past family again: once the negative is formed, ない → なかった works for all three verb families. Even 行く starts from 行かない, not 行った.

Decide two features: whether the action is affirmed or denied, and whether it is past or non-past. All four forms in each table are valid but express different things. 食べた is not a grammatical error when you wanted 食べなかった: it is an answer with the wrong polarity.
grammar.v2.adjective-adverb-ku-ni.title: Describing how an action is done
grammar.v2.adjective-adverb-ku-ni.summar: In the い group replace い with く: 早い → 早く. In the な group add に: 静か → 静かに. These forms describe how the action is performed.
grammar.v2.adjective-adverb-ku-ni.goal: Turn adjective descriptions into ways of performing an action.
grammar.v2.adjective-adverb-ku-ni.idea: In the い group replace い with く: 早い → 早く. In the な group add に: 静か → 静かに. These forms describe how the action is performed.
grammar.v2.adjective-adverb-ku-ni.exampl: A fast person, depending on context
grammar.v2.adjective-adverb-ku-ni.detail: Ask what you are describing. 静かな人 modifies the noun 人 and uses the な link from Topic 02. 静かに話す describes the manner of speaking and uses に. This に belongs to the adverbial pattern; we do not teach its other uses as a verbal particle here.

早い人 and 早く歩く distinguish a person’s quality from a way of walking. Not all Japanese adverbs are built from an adjective: とても and ぜんぜん are already independent forms. These two rules apply to adjectives in the groups you know.
grammar.v2.adjective-adverb-ku-ni.contra: な links to a noun; に expresses the manner of the action.
い modifies the noun; く allows the action to be described.

grammar.v2.topic03-review-09.explanation: Decide the group and ending family before building the past.

grammar.v2.topic03-review-10.explanation: Decide the group and ending family before building the past.
